title: On the number of conjugacy classes of finite solvable groups of order divisible by $p^2$
summary: In 2003, Héthelyi and Külshammer proved that if $G$ is a finite solvable group and $p$ is a prime such that $p^2$ divides $|G|$, then $k(G)\geq (49p+1)/60$, and they constructed an infinite family of groups for which this bound was claimed to be attained. We point out that the groups in this family are not Frobenius groups, so that their class numbers are considerably larger than stated, and that in fact the bound is never attained.
